title: Granular PR audit + follow-ups (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- PR 4289 is a cross-cutting refactor touching handler routing, kv-cache glue, and the nvbench harness integration. Landing this will affect latency SLIs and a few deprecated API shapes we still support for v0 customers.
- Quick goal for this scratchpad: capture micro-checks to run during review, list potential follow-ups (post-merge), and log small experiments to validate regressions before canary.

Quick high-level checklist (run this during review):
- API contract
  - Ensure public handlers keep backward compatible request fields (trace_id, client_version).
  - Migration note: remove legacy "session_token" param is documented in INF-2026 (do not remove until 30 days after rollout).
- Tests
  - Unit: each modified module has >80% coverage for new branches. 
  - Integration: local integration harness passes with kv-cache warmup for 3 different sequence lengths: 32, 128, 1024.
  - E2E: smoketest via local devstack: basic generate/chat path + force-streaming scenario.
- Performance / Benchmarks
  - Run nvbench microbench for attention kernel path (baseline vs branch). Expect <5% latency regression on 512-seq; flag otherwise.
  - Throughput smoke: 100 concurrent tiny requests (seq <=64) and 10 concurrent long requests (seq 1024) to observe batching behavior changes.
- Correctness
  - KV cache parity: replay cached sessions from fixtures (fixtures/cache-replay/*). 5 sample conversations should produce identical tokens for first 40 tokens.
  - Stochastic outputs: seeds consistent where set; add a deterministic-mode test for the new path.
- Observability / Telemetry
  - Ensure new code emits route tags for sampling (route=redwood.v2.refactor).
  - Validate error traces show original stack (no swallow/transform that hides root cause).
- Security / Surface area
  - No inline secrets or hardcoded file paths.
  - Confirm new dependency (token-utils v2.1.0) has no known CVEs (check Snyk report).

Notes-to-self (things to call out in review comments):
- lines 312-330: handler multiplexing looks clever but complicates metric attribution. Suggest adding a static field to the request context that is populated early and used by metrics instead of inferring from route later.
- module caching: if we change import order on startup it may affect passive memory usage (observed +120MB on my local laptop). Add one-liner in PR description to call this out.
- consider moving the `kv_cache.py` small helper functions into a package-level utils; right now they have mixed responsibility (serialize vs metrics).
- the retry/backoff decorator default (backoff=0.2 -> 3 retries) is risky for low-latency paths. Recommend default 1 retry for generate path and document in readme.

Follow-ups (post-merge tasks):
- INF-XXXX: canonicalize request context field and migrate metrics plumbing. (owner: Evan)
- Add a canary config in cluster routing to route 5% traffic to the refactor branch for 48 hours with extended logging. (owner: Maya)
- Run quantized-model smoke (if landing impacts kernel selection) to ensure int8 path still matches qualitative quality thresholds.
- Audit dashboards for SLO drift: create alert for >3% p50 increase vs baseline for 24h.

Small experiments to run before canary:
- A/B bench: baseline vs branch with sequence-length-distribution file (perf/seq-dist/last-week.json). Collate median latency diffs per model.
- Cold-start path: restart a pod and run 10 sequential long sessions to measure KV warmup time.
- Sampling impact: enable debug sampling at 0.1% for 2 hours and inspect sample size for the new route tag.

Review comment templates (copy & paste):
- "Nice refactor — good separation. Can you add a short comment on why we choose X over Y (perf tradeoff) so future reviewers don't remove this?"
- "This change affects metric attribution; please add a small unit test that asserts the new request context field is populated."
- "Observed a potential memory regression locally (~120MB). Can you run a heap profile and add the snapshot to the PR?"

Risk register (quick):
- High: latency regression for long-seq workloads (mitigate via canary + fallback to previous handler).
- Medium: metrics attribution gaps (mitigate with explicit field + migration).
- Low: small test flakes due to seeding; add deterministic-mode tests.

Estimated review time: 60–90 minutes (deep pass), extra 30 minutes for running local nvbench and caches.

Final quick checklist before approve: 
[ ] Unit + integration tests green
[ ] nvbench <=5% regression on kernel path (or documented reason)
[ ] Observability tags present
[ ] Post-merge tasks filed in Jira
[ ] Canary plan attached in PR description

Misc scratch notes / random thoughts:
- I want a small script that runs the three perf scenarios and uploads results to a PR comment; could reuse parts of infra/scripts/bench_commenter.py.
- Keep an eye on dependency bump for token-utils; maybe pin to minor in the short term.
- If landing causes a regression, fallback should be a runtime flag not require code rollback (we already have the route-policy plumbing — check integration tests for toggle).

End of scratchpad.
summary: Personal scratchpad for PR 4289: micro-checklist, follow-ups, experiments, and review comment templates.
